metadata.case_name: LAM MEI WAN v. NGAI KEUNG JAMES AND ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: janitor with SKH Lam Kau Mow Secondary School

source: Radiograph showed fracture of the coccyx.

The plaintiff sustained coccygeal fracture in the Accident, which was compatible and consistent with the mechanism of injury given by the plaintiff that her fracture was solely attributable to the Accident.
injuries.icd_description: Other specified fracture of lumbar spine or pelvis

injuries.description: pre-existing spondylosis of the cervical and lumbar spine, and reduced C5/6 disc space with narrowing of intervertebral foramina
source: It was also observed that the plaintiff had pre-existing spondylosis of the cervical and lumbar spine, and reduced C5/6 disc space with narrowing of intervertebral foramina.
There is no dispute that before the Accident, the plaintiff suffered workplace injuries on 23 December 2011 during the course of her employment with the School (the "Previous Accident").

manifestations.description: right lower limb pain and numbness (complained at times but not found on 2017 examination)
mild weakness of both lower limbs
midline tender spot over the sacrococcygeal region and bilateral paraspinal muscle tenderness
range of lumbar motion: flexion 60 degrees, extension 10 degrees, lateral flexion 20 degrees
positive Waddell's simulation tests (indication of presence of nonorganic causes of back pain)

treatments_received.treatment: ambulance transfer to Accident and Emergency Department of Ruttonjee Hospital
source: The plaintiff was then taken by ambulance to the Accident and Emergency Department of Ruttonjee Hospital for treatment.

treatments_received.treatment: intramuscular analgesic and conservative management with analgesics
source: She was given intramuscular analgesic and admitted to the Orthopaedic Department of Pamela Youde Nethersole Eastern Hospital ("PYH") for further examination.
The plaintiff's fracture was managed conservatively with analgesics.
The plaintiff was thereafter referred to physiotherapy and occupational therapy. Such treatment was standard and appropriate.

losses.description: Residual coccygeal pain and reduced endurance especially on prolonged walking, standing, climbing or squatting; coccygeal discomfort on prolonged sitting

comparable_cases.case_name: Chan Yuk King v Tung Chun
comparable_cases.injury_description: X-ray showed that she suffered from a fracture of her coccyx; plaintiff also suffered from a S4 fracture; if back pain it should be of a minor nature
